summary: Adds three planted-bug eval fixtures for the debug-loop skill, each a small Python module plus pytest tests. expired-sessions: append-only session store where get_session picks the newest row by one-second created_at. pricing-regression: line_total rounds with Python round(), tests expect half-cent rounds up. slow-enrichment: enrich_orders does a linear scan per order over a copied customer list; run_nightly times 20000x20000 to expose the O(n*m) cost. Tests are light and mostly pass.

claims.text: get_session returns the row with the max created_at; ties between same-second rows resolve arbitrarily rather than by version.
refresh returns 404 for unknown session, 401 when expires_at <= now, else 200 with token.
line_total uses Python round(), which is banker's rounding on floats; test expects 1.995 to bill as 2.00.
enrich_orders scans the full customer list per order, O(orders*customers).
run_nightly builds 20000 customers and 20000 orders and prints elapsed seconds.
Unknown customer_id yields customer=None and order fields are preserved.

risks.note: Docstring promises version ordering; max by created_at ignores version on same-second refresh. Tests never cover tie.
Float 0.70*3*0.95 may not equal exactly 1.995; round() result depends on float repr, test may fail.
index_customers only copies dicts; name implies index but builds none. Intentional planted slowness.

least_confident: Whether round(0.70*3*0.95, 2) actually yields 2.00 or 1.99 in CPython, which decides if the pricing test is the intended planted failure.
